title: Curated place entry
description: One entry in data/places.mumbai.json. The schema exists to make fabrication a validation failure rather than a matter of good intentions: coordinates cannot carry a value without machine provenance, and any claim-bearing field must be reachable from the sources array.

id.description: Stable slug. Never reused, never renamed once shipped — place_visits rows reference it.

name_local.description: Marathi/Hindi/Gujarati name in its own script, where the place is actually known by one. Null when it genuinely has no local-script name in common use — not a machine transliteration of the English.

geo.description: OSM-derived once resolved, and therefore published under ODbL separately from the editorial fields. lat/lng MUST stay null until tools/resolve_geo.py fills them from a real OSM lookup — the validator rejects a coordinate without provenance. This is the anti-fabrication mechanism: a plausible-looking coordinate 400 m off the right lane is a fabricated address in every way that matters.

osm_query.description: The search string that resolves this place. Written to be unambiguous enough that a human can check the pin landed on the building, not the neighbourhood centroid.

source.description: e.g. 'osm:node/1234567890' or 'osm:way/98765'. Required whenever lat/lng are non-null.

what_it_is.description: Concrete and specific. Adjectives are not substance: 'iconic', 'vibrant', 'hidden gem' and 'must-visit' are rejected by the validator.

insider_rules.description: The ordering ritual, the cash-only fact, the counter to go to, the permission to ask. This is the product; it renders above the photo.

always_open.description: True for public streets, maidans and seafronts — places with no gate and therefore no opening hour. Distinct from 'hours known to be 00:00-24:00', and it needs no citation: the useful information for these is a time of day, carried in best_time and crowd_level_by_time.

opens_at.description: Use when the opening time is verified but the closing time is not. Half a fact is still a fact; inventing the other half to fill a window object is not. The app renders 'opens 05:00 · closing time unverified'.

months.description: Months in which this is worth doing at all. An entry outside its season is hidden or visibly de-ranked, never silently shown — the Sewri flamingos are a Nov-Mar entry and showing them in August sends you to an empty mudflat.

avg_paise.description: Integer paise, never a float. Null when not verified — an unverified price ships empty, it does not ship as a guess.

monsoon_safe.description: yes = indoor or covered, works in a downpour. conditional = fine in light rain, miserable or closed in heavy. no = do not plan this in August.

safety_notes.description: Includes solo, after-dark and women's-safety observations where relevant. Never reassuring by default — 'unknown, assess on arrival' is an acceptable and often more honest value.

pairs_with.description: Nearby entry ids. Validator rejects ids that do not exist — this is what makes 'build my day' possible.

underrated_basis.description: The brief's filter: an entry qualifies only if at least two of these hold. Enforced by minItems, so a tourist-trap default cannot pass validation without someone lying in the data.

confidence_note.description: Required for medium and low. Says exactly which field is shaky and why, so the app can render 'hours unverified' rather than a false certainty.
